events.text: Rooms the sea once held — an original imagined nautilus shell on dark sand, sparked by Aquarium of the Pacific: https://www.aquariumofpacific.org/onlinelearningcenter/species/chambered_nautilus . AI painter. Goal: broad joined warm shell planes before unequal quiet ribs, with one compact rim light.
The first wash leaves pale lanes between long gestures. Broad bridges will join the field before the shell is placed.
The background is joined, with faint wash bands retained. A broad warm mass and low contact shadow will establish the shell before pattern.
The outline left a large blue center and a small opening pinhole. Crossed broad planes will fill those gaps before a spiral is drawn.
Cross planes filled most of the center but left two blue flecks and raised seams. One loaded interior bridge will close them; a dark opening can then turn the lower lip.
The opening reads, but one blue center fleck survived the thin cover. A loaded short plane will close it; the spiral should remain quieter than the rim.
The spiral is readable but faceted, and the crown light is broad. I will use more closely sampled curves for the warm ribs and leave gaps between their unequal widths.
Four warm ribs turn across the crown, though their roots are blunt. Lower ribs can be shorter and quieter to keep the upper-left light dominant.
The ribs read as spokes. Wider light planes alongside selected ribs should make the surface turn without tracing every stripe.
The curved light planes shortened some ribs but left ledges. A finer inner coil and restrained pale side can reduce the diagram-like center.
The smaller coil is gentler, but the old broad spiral remains angular. I will keep that irregularity for now and establish two quiet stones to anchor the shell.
The pale crown needs one compact accent, not a continuous bright outline. I will test a short loaded rim light alone.
The short rim light survives whole view. The stones remain quiet; the right center needs a broad fill before any small cracks.
Upper review: the rim light is compact, while broad spiral facets and regular bristle relief remain. I will preserve the light as quieter foreground gestures are added.
The kelp reads as stiff bent prongs. More sampled flowing paths should soften their gestures; longer leaves can cross the low stem without approaching the focal light.
The kelp curves are gentler but old elbows remain. The cast shadow is a dark rail; thin blue oil along its ends and lower edge may integrate it with the sand.
The thin cover spread the shadow into wider blue rails rather than softening it. I will shorten the outer ends with matching sand color and keep the failed relief visible in the record.
Shadow covers only partly changed color and left relief. The warm lower plane joined better. Refinement will now clarify aperture thickness and quiet selected stripe roots.
The lip is clearer, and root covers shortened the upper stripes but left light patches. Quiet stone planes and two uneven kelp veins can finish the foreground without competing with the shell.
Lower review: checking kelp joins, stone contact and the retained raised shadow patches.

The lower review confirms broad raised blue rails below the shadow and a broken-looking kelp fork. I will test one more loaded cover on the outer rail, then reconnect the fork with a short warm-green overlap.
The loaded test changed color only slightly and retained ridges. A few broad shell bridges will address interior seams; further ground covers would likely add relief.
Broad bridges reduced some seam contrast but broke the upper-left spiral connection. A thin sampled repair will reconnect that turn, with a quieter lower coil.

The sampled repair reconnects the spiral more gently, while broad roots and raised cover seams remain. Final refinement: restore the compact rim light, join its neighboring plane, and quiet the aperture and kelp accents.

Final review at 88 completed marks: broad overlaps filled most of the shell; sampled spiral repair is gentler and one compact rim light holds focus. A small cool center fleck, faceted crown, blunt stripe roots, stiff kelp elbows, regular bristles and raised blue shadow covers remain. Stopping because further covers would likely add relief rather than clarify the form.
